decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom serves a growing, specialized niche where few rivals compete, it supports the platform strategy, and its value has not yet played out after the delayed US release, so the option stays open at low holding cost.

Small-field dosimetry demand keeps rising with stereotactic and MR-linac treatments, ionization chambers have long life cycles, and keeping a catalog chamber costs little, so there is no reason to abandon it.
Although it partly overlaps with B, the second small volume chamber covers a different detector size and use case, carrying it is cheap, and there is no clear evidence that it fails to capture value.
The relative dosimetry chamber complements the water phantom systems and the scanning workflow, which keeps it tied to core sales at minimal maintenance cost.
Thimble chambers are established workhorse devices with steady, predictable demand and accredited calibration support, so the product has proven its value and should be kept.
